data.short_meaning: God of wealth, prosperity and power
data.long_meaning: Lakshmana is the younger brother of Lord Rama and is known as the God of wealth, prosperity, and strength. He is the embodiment of moral values and is considered a role model of loyalty and devotion. The name Lakhn carries the meaning “God of wealth, prosperity and power” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit. Parents who choose Lakhn usually hope their child will grow to embody god of wealth, prosperity and power and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Lakhn total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

data.cultural_impact: Lakshmana, also spelled as Lakhn or Laxman, is a popular name among Hindus, especially in India and Nepal. The name Lakshmana is derived from Sanskrit language and means 'protected by wealth' or 'bountiful'. Lakshmana is revered as the younger brother of Lord Rama and is considered a crucial figure in the Indian epic Ramayana. He is known as Lord Vishnu's avatar and is often worshipped as a deity, particularly in the form of a protective Siras-Savitri yantra.
data.spiritual_significance: In Hinduism, Lakshmana represents moral values, loyalty, courage, strength, and courage. He is considered an embodiment of Rama's younger brother and is often seen as a role model of devotion and sacrifice. Lakshmana's most notable act of devotion is his vow to protect his brother Lord Rama and his wife Sita at all costs. This vow is symbolized by the Shivaree yantra, worn as a protective talisman.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Lakhn, derived from the Sanskrit word "Lakshman," symbolizes protection and purity. It is a name of Lord Vishnu, representing his unwavering support and shield against evil. This name conveys a sense of security and spiritual strength.
